annotation_description: Citadel Siege is one of the strongest cards available for this +1/+1 counter-themed deck, synergizing with Champion of Lambholt, Fathom Mage, and Elite Scaleguard. It provides two +1/+1 counters per combat. The hand already has two Plains available from the choices to help cast it.

message: Select a card (1 more) to put on the bottom of your library
annotation_description: Misleading Signpost is actually a useful card in this hand - it's a flash artifact that taps for {U} (serving as mana rock), and has a defensive combat trick ability. With only 3 lands in a 7-card hand (Island, Swamp, Tainted Isle) plus Temple of the False God which needs 5 lands to activate, the Signpost would help with mana development. Temple of the False God is the weakest card here since it's a dead card until you have 5 lands, which will take many turns. With Wayfarer's Bauble for ramp and only 3 functional lands, Temple is unlikely to be activated quickly.

message: Select a card (2 more) to put on the bottom of your library
annotation_description: Haiku Valley bottomed both Swamps from a hand that appears to contain only Swamps as lands. With a hand of Perplexing Test (5 mana), Thrilling Encore (5 mana), Distant Melody (4 mana), Oona (6 mana), and Faerie Seer (1 mana), keeping zero lands means they cannot cast anything except possibly Faerie Seer if they draw a land. In a multiplayer game starting turn 1, having no lands in hand is catastrophic - they'll need to draw into lands naturally and will likely miss early land drops, falling far behind.

Etherium Sculptor would have enabled significantly better tempo: it makes Emry cost just {U} (affinity from Sculptor as an artifact + Sculptor's cost reduction), and Prodigy's Prototype cost {W}{U} instead of {1}{W}{U}. This would allow deploying the entire artifact-heavy hand much faster. Sram draws cards off Swift Reconfiguration and Prodigy's Prototype, but the tempo advantage of Sculptor with this specific hand (Emry + Prototype) seems stronger.

The player's reasoning claims Emry draws a card on cast and Sram triggers for another card, but this is incorrect. Sram only triggers on casting Aura, Equipment, or Vehicle spells — not creature spells like Emry. Additionally, Emry mills four cards on ETB rather than drawing. The player also has no artifacts in the graveyard to recur with Emry's tap ability, making her less immediately useful. Etherium Sculptor would have reduced future artifact costs (including Prodigy's Prototype and Mind Stone), providing better mana efficiency going forward, and could have enabled casting Prodigy's Prototype next turn more easily. However, Emry is still a reasonable play as a body that mills and could enable future recursion if artifacts end up in the graveyard.

Mind Stone is the better play here on turn 3. Haiku Valley has Archmage of Echoes (5 mana) in hand, and ramping with Mind Stone gets them closer to casting it sooner. With Dimir Signet already on board, Mind Stone would give them 5 mana sources next turn (3 lands + Signet + Mind Stone), potentially enabling a turn 4 Archmage of Echoes which is a much more powerful play. Mocking Sprite is a 2/1 flyer that provides minimal pressure in a 4-player game at 40 life. The spell cost reduction from Mocking Sprite is minor compared to the ramp value of Mind Stone toward the powerful 5-drop.

Chose Verdant Embrace over Mantle of the Ancients despite having a hand full of Auras (Giant Inheritance, Sage's Reverie) and Winds of Rath. Mantle of the Ancients would scale enormously with multiple Auras, trigger Siona multiple times when recurring Auras from graveyard, and provide resilience after Winds of Rath (which destroys non-enchanted creatures but may cause Aura losses later). Sage's Reverie would also draw more cards with Mantle enabling more Auras on board.

Attacking with Emry (1/2) for a measly 1 damage means she's tapped and can't use her tap ability to recur an artifact from the graveyard. The graveyard contains Gold Myr and Smuggler's Copter, both castable with available mana. Recurring either artifact would provide significantly more value than 1 point of damage.

message: Select a player, planeswalker, or battle to attack
annotation_description: Attacking Kimi25 Dreamer who has multiple untapped blockers (Sanctum Weaver, Human Monk Token, Siona) that can block or trade, when Haiku Valley has their only creature (Mocking Sprite) tapped, guaranteeing unblocked damage.

message: Select up to one card to cast
annotation_description: Retether only returns Aura cards from the graveyard, and the graveyard contains only a single Careful Cultivation. The player hallucinated having multiple powerful Auras in their graveyard. Retether for one aura is significantly worse than casting Primal Vigor (doubles tokens and counters for rest of game, synergizing with Siona and the entire enchantment strategy) or Ajani's Chosen (creates 2/2 tokens on every enchantment ETB) for free.

Casting Smuggler's Copter during the combat phase instead of main phase 1 means they cannot crew and attack with it this turn, missing 3 flying damage and a loot trigger (draw + discard). Sram (2 power) could have crewed it (crew 1) and they could have attacked.

The player's reasoning identified Rankle, Master of Pranks as 'SO good for removal' and 'amazing for board control,' yet they cast Nettling Nuisance instead. With available mana (Island, Island, Swamp, Dimir Signet, Arcane Signet, Darkwater Catacombs = at least 4 mana of various colors including BB), Rankle (2BB) was castable and is a significantly stronger card. Rankle has haste allowing immediate combat damage, and its triggered ability (each player discards/loses life/sacrifices) provides much more disruption against the board state where Kimi25 Dreamer has a large enchanted creature and Qwen3L Pessim has key utility creatures. Nettling Nuisance is a 3/1 flyer with no haste that needs to connect before generating value. The reasoning contradicts the action taken.

Kimi25 Dreamer has a Plains in hand and an untapped Plains on the battlefield, but chose to do nothing this turn. They missed their land drop (playing Plains) which would give them 4 mana sources plus Sanctum Weaver. With the land drop, they could have cast Arcane Signet (2 mana) to ramp, or Spectral Steel on Siona to draw a card off Enchantress's Presence and buff their creature, or Umbra Mystic (3 mana with the extra land). Additionally, they have 8 cards in hand and will have to discard to 7 at end of turn, meaning they're literally throwing away a card for free. At minimum, playing the Plains and casting Arcane Signet would develop their board and avoid the discard.

Kimi25 Dreamer discarded Arcane Signet instead of Plains when forced to discard to hand size. With Sanctum Weaver already on the battlefield (which taps for mana equal to enchantments controlled), and Enchantress's Presence and Sage's Reverie already in play, the player has good mana production. However, Arcane Signet is a 2-mana rock that provides color fixing and ramp when cast, while Plains is a basic land that only taps for one white mana. The player already has 3 Plains on the battlefield. Given the enchantment-heavy deck with cards like Primal Vigor (4G), Umbra Mystic (2W), and Spectral Steel (1W) still in hand, having an additional mana rock would help cast multiple spells per turn. A basic Plains is less valuable than a mana artifact when you already have 3 Plains and Sanctum Weaver for mana production. That said, with Sanctum Weaver scaling with enchantments, the Arcane Signet's relative value is somewhat diminished, making this a close call.

GPT5m Rules chose Blue mana (likely from Exotic Orchard) when they already have an Island for blue mana. They critically need Black mana to cast Reyhan, Last of the Abzan ({1}{B}{G}) this turn, and Black is also needed for Duneblast later. With Black from Exotic Orchard plus their existing Forest and other lands, they could cast Reyhan immediately.

Kimi25 Dreamer claims 'Just Siona is lethal damage to Qwen3L' but Siona is a 2/2 attacking into a player at 16 life - that's not remotely lethal. Attacking with only Siona deals 2 damage (assuming no blocks) instead of sending a much larger force to apply meaningful pressure.

Duneblast is GPT5m Rules' most powerful spell in hand - a 7-mana board wipe that lets you keep your best creature. With Kimi25 Dreamer building an enchantress engine (Sanctum Weaver, Siona, Enchantress's Presence, Sage's Reverie) and GPT5m Rules having a relatively weak board position, Duneblast would be a critical answer to recover from falling behind. The discard appears to be from Rankle's combat damage trigger (each player discards a card). While the hand has many lands that could be discarded instead, GPT5m Rules chose to discard their best card. They have 5 lands in hand (Terramorphic Expanse, Evolving Wilds, Plains, Seaside Citadel, Arcane Sanctum) and only 4 lands on the battlefield - but they could easily discard one of the taplands or a basic Plains while keeping their most impactful spell.

message: Choose spell or ability to playCloud of Faeries
annotation_description: Casting Cloud of Faeries before Archmage of Echoes means missing out on the Archmage's copy trigger. If Archmage of Echoes were cast first (5 mana), then Cloud of Faeries (2 mana), the Archmage would copy Cloud of Faeries, creating an extra 1/1 flying token and untapping additional lands. This would also potentially enable casting Rankle in the same turn with the untapped lands.

Kimi25 Dreamer has a 33/35 Siona (enchanted with Sage's Reverie giving massive stats) and only two opponents remain. Primal Vigor is a symmetrical doubling effect that helps ALL players' tokens and +1/+1 counters - notably GPT5m Rules has Custodi Soulbinders (which makes tokens and uses +1/+1 counters) and Fathom Mage (which draws cards from +1/+1 counters). Meanwhile, Kimi25 already has a dominant board position with a huge creature. Playing Primal Vigor helps opponents more than it helps the player who is already winning. More critically, Winds of Rath would destroy all non-enchanted creatures, wiping opponents' boards while preserving their own enchanted Siona - this would likely set up lethal attacks. Playing Primal Vigor before combat also means not attacking with the 33/35 Siona this turn before doing anything else.

Cast Sol Ring before playing a land for the turn. While the end result is likely the same, playing a land first (Forest) would give maximum mana flexibility and follows proper sequencing principles. With Forest + Sanctum Weaver (3 mana) = 4 mana available, casting Sol Ring and then potentially Umbra Mystic in the same turn would be cleaner with land played first.

Kimi25 Dreamer cast Umbra Mystic (a 2/2 with incremental protection) instead of Winds of Rath, which would have been a one-sided board wipe. Siona with Sage's Reverie is enchanted and would survive Winds of Rath, while all of GPT5m Rules' creatures (Fathom Mage, Custodi Soulbinders, Spirit Token) and Haiku Valley's Mocking Sprite would be destroyed. With 6 mana available (3 Plains + Forest + Sanctum Weaver for 2), they had exactly enough for Winds of Rath's {3}{W}{W} cost.

Solidarity of Heroes costs {1}{G} and targets creatures with +1/+1 counters to double them. Looking at the board, Custodi Soulbinders and Fathom Mage likely have +1/+1 counters, so doubling them could be valuable. However, this is being cast in response to Siona entering the battlefield on the opponent's (Kimi25 Dreamer's) turn. The trigger on the stack is Siona's ETB (look at top 7 for an Aura). Solidarity of Heroes doesn't interact with or counter this trigger at all - it just doubles +1/+1 counters on GPT5m's own creatures. While doubling counters has value, spending this combat trick at sorcery-speed timing during the opponent's turn beginning phase wastes it when it could be saved for a more impactful moment - like before attacks to make blockers bigger, or in response to removal, or combined with Fathom Mage to draw many cards at a more strategic time. Additionally, casting it now when Siona is on the stack means Custodi Soulbinders won't count Siona for its counter total (Siona hasn't resolved yet). More importantly, this uses up 2 mana ({1}{G}) that could be used for other responses, and Solidarity of Heroes is a one-shot spell being used without clear strategic urgency.

annotation_description: Haiku Valley has 0 cards in hand, meaning 'Each player discards a card' would be asymmetrically beneficial - opponents lose cards while Haiku Valley loses nothing. This free value mode was not selected alongside the sacrifice mode. Additionally, the sacrifice mode forces Haiku Valley to sacrifice one of their own creatures (likely Mocking Sprite), while GPT5m Rules can just sacrifice a Spirit token (minimal loss).

Treasure Cruise has Delve, and GPT5m Rules has 7 cards in their graveyard already, meaning it could be cast for just U (or close to it). At 14 life with a relatively weak board, drawing 3 cards for essentially 1 mana would be extremely valuable. Meanwhile, there are several less impactful cards to discard - lands like Terramorphic Expanse, Evolving Wilds, Seaside Citadel, or Arcane Sanctum (tapped lands) that are far less valuable than a near-free draw-3 spell.

message: Select up to one attacking creature
annotation_description: Declined to activate Spectral Steel's graveyard ability ({1}{W}, exile from graveyard to return an Aura from graveyard to hand). Kenrith's Transformation is in the graveyard and would be a valuable recovery - it serves as removal that also draws a card. With 4 untapped mana available and only needing 2 for the activation, this is essentially free value.

Kimi25 Dreamer passed priority during combat without activating Spectral Steel's exile ability from the graveyard ({1}{W}, exile to return another Aura from graveyard to hand). With Kenrith's Transformation and other Auras in the graveyard, this would have been free value - especially valuable in a 1v1 situation against the last remaining opponent.
